# BP 344 Accessible Ramp Geometry

## Learning objective

Given a ramp condition in an LEA plan-reading or code-compliance question, identify the governing accessible-ramp values for width, gradient, landing, and handrail height under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344.

## The rule that decides the answer

An accessible ramp starts with two values: a minimum clear width of 1200 mm and a gradient not steeper than 1:20. The same 2024 BP 344 IRR excerpt allows steeper gradients only as special cases depending on the length to be covered.

Source: BP 344, 2024 Revised IRR, Appendix A, Accessible Ramps, PDF p.2, extracted from `vitruvius-connection/001_Raw-Source-Layer/001-Laws/BP-344/2024 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations Batas Pambansa Blg. 344 _ National Council on Disability Affairs.pdf`.

## How the table is tested

The table row for 1:15 permits a 10.50 m maximum length, a 700 mm maximum rise, and a 10 m interval for landing. The same page states that accessible ramps with a total length longer than 10.50 m must be provided with intermediate landings with a minimum length of 1800 mm.

Source: BP 344, 2024 Revised IRR, Appendix A, Accessible Ramps, Table A.1.1 and Item 10, PDF p.2.

## Handrail trap

For accessible ramps with changes in grade higher than 170 mm, handrails are required. They must be on both sides, and they are installed at 900 mm and 700 mm above ramps and stairs. Do not answer only one height when the stem asks for accessible ramp handrails.

# RA 9266 Foreign Architect and Temporary Permit Gate

## Learning objective

Given a professional-practice scenario involving a foreign architect, identify whether the person may lawfully perform architectural services in the Philippines and which RA 9266 IRR requirement controls the answer.

## Definitions that come first

The RA 9266 IRR defines a foreign architect as an architect who is not a Filipino citizen and is not registered and licensed in the Philippines, but is duly registered and licensed in the architect's home country. It also defines the Filipino counterpart as the local Philippine architect, partnership, or corporation that must work in association with the foreign architect, partnership, or corporation on a project on Philippine soil.

Source: RA 9266 IRR, Section 3, Definition of Terms, Items 30 and 31, PDF p.5, extracted from `vitruvius-connection/001_Raw-Source-Layer/001-Laws/RA-9266/RA-9266 IRR Architecture Act of 2004.pdf`.

## The permit gate

Section 38 is the exam hinge. A foreign national who enters the Philippines to perform professional services as an architect or consultant in the covered projects must secure a special/temporary permit from the Board, subject to approval of the Commission, before assuming the duties, functions, and responsibilities as architect or consultant.

Source: RA 9266 IRR, Section 38, Coverage of Temporary/Special Permits, PDF p.20.

## Board shortcut

Being licensed abroad is not the same as authority to practice architecture in the Philippines. In an LEA stem, check three gates: home-country licensure, Filipino counterpart, and special/temporary permit approval. If any gate is missing, the option that treats foreign licensure alone as sufficient is wrong.

# RA 9514 Means of Egress: Width, Count, and Illumination

## Learning objective

Given a Fire Code egress stem, decide whether the issue is exit sufficiency, minimum egress width, number of means of egress, or illumination.

## The life-safety premise

The 2019 Revised IRR of RA 9514 requires every building or structure designed for human occupancy to have exits sufficient to permit fast and safe escape in case of fire or other emergencies. The same general requirement states that exits must be appropriate in kind, number, location, and capacity for the occupancy, exposed population, fire protection, height, and construction type.

Source: RA 9514, 2019 Revised IRR, Rule 10, Chapter 2, Division 2, General Requirements, PDF p.89, extracted from `vitruvius-connection/001_Raw-Source-Layer/001-Laws/RA-9514/RA9514-RIRR-rev-2019.pdf`.

## Width and number are separate checks

For the general means-of-egress rule, the width of any means of egress must not be less than 915 mm unless Divisions 8 through 20 provide a specific exception. The number of means of egress from any balcony, mezzanine, storey, or portion must not be less than two, except where those same occupancy divisions specifically permit otherwise.

Source: RA 9514, 2019 Revised IRR, Rule 10, Chapter 2, Section 10.2.5.2, paragraphs F and G, PDF p.95.

## Load threshold trap

If the occupant load for any storey or portion is more than 500 but not more than 1000, the means of egress must not be less than three. If it is in excess of 1000, the means of egress must not be less than four. Do not confuse this count rule with the 915 mm minimum-width rule.

# National Plumbing Code Fixture Units and Venting

## Learning objective

Use the National Plumbing Code definition of fixture unit and the Code rule on vent piping to avoid common utilities distractors.

## Fixture unit is a load measure

The Revised National Plumbing Code defines fixture unit as an arbitrary quantity used to express the load-producing effects or water requirements of different plumbing fixtures. One fixture unit is equivalent to a rate of flow of 28.3 liters per minute, which is 1 cubic foot per minute.

Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Definitions, Fixture Unit, PDF p.24, extracted from `vitruvius-connection/001_Raw-Source-Layer/005-Utilities/Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.pdf`.

## Venting is not spare drainage

The same Code prohibits using a vent pipe as a soil or waste pipe, and prohibits using a soil or waste pipe as a vent, except as otherwise provided in Sections 812, 813, and 814. It also states that single drainage and venting systems with unvented branch lines are prohibited.

Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Section 311.4, PDF p.44.

## Loop or circuit vent

A loop or circuit vent is a vertical vent connection on a horizontal soil or waste branch downstream of the last fixture connection, turning to a horizontal line above the highest overflow level of the highest connected fixture.

# Vitruvius: Principles versus Departments of Architecture

## Learning objective

Distinguish Vitruvius's fundamental principles of architecture from his departments of architecture, so an LEA theory stem does not trap you with the wrong list.

## The principles list

In Book I, Chapter II, Vitruvius states that architecture depends on Order, Arrangement, Eurythmy, Symmetry, Propriety, and Economy. He defines eurythmy as beauty and fitness in the adjustments of the members, and symmetry as the agreement between the members of the work and the relation between parts and the whole.

Source: Vitruvius, Ten Books on Architecture, translated by Morris Hicky Morgan, Book I, Chapter II, PDF pp.33-34, extracted from `vitruvius-connection/001_Raw-Source-Layer/002-History/Vitruvius - 10 Books of Architecture.pdf`.

## Economy is not just cheapness

Vitruvius describes economy as proper management of materials and site, with a thrifty balancing of cost and common sense in construction. In exam terms, do not reduce economy to minimum cost. It is fit use of resources under real site and supply constraints.

Source: Vitruvius, Ten Books on Architecture, Book I, Chapter II, PDF p.36.

## The departments list

In Book I, Chapter III, Vitruvius says there are three departments of architecture: the art of building, the making of time-pieces, and the construction of machinery. Building is then divided into fortified towns and public works on one side, and structures for private individuals on the other.
